title: King Leonidas I of Sparta
biography: Agiad King of Sparta whose heroic stand with 300 Spartan warriors and Greek allies at the Battle of Thermopylae against Xerxes' massive Persian invasion became an eternal symbol of courage.
internationalConnections: Commanded the unified Greek land forces defending against the Achaemenid Persian invasion.

title: King Jaya Sinha
biography: Jaya Sinha ruled Jaffna for seven years, maintaining Hindu patronage and northern trade. His brief reign continued the dynasty's policies of temple-building and irrigation maintenance, sustaining Jaffna's maritime prosperity amid regional volatility.

title: King Anikanga
biography: Anikanga (1209) held power momentarily, ruling less than a year. His ultrashort tenure exemplifies the extreme instability preceding Polonnaruwa's abandonment. Succession contestation dominated political life, precluding governance effectiveness.

title: King Ethirimana Cinkam
biography: Ethirimana Cinkam ruled Jaffna for 26 years amid intensifying Portuguese demands. He attempted to balance loyalty to the Portuguese with the preservation of Tamil Hindu culture. His reign saw shrinking autonomy and foreshadowed the kingdom's eventual annexation.

title: Sundiata Keita (The Lion King of Mali)
biography: Founder of the Mali Empire who defeated the Sosso king Sumanguru Kante at the Battle of Kirina and proclaimed the Kouroukan Fouga, one of the world's earliest constitutional charters of human rights.
internationalConnections: Unified the Mandinka clans and secured the trans-Saharan gold-salt trade routes.

title: King Asela
biography: Asela was a king of the Anuradhapura Kingdom who heroically restored the Vijayan dynasty after a period of foreign rule. He was the youngest of the nine sons of King Mutasiva. After the two Tamil invaders, Sena and Guttika, had ruled for 22 years, Asela raised an army, defeated them in battle, and reclaimed the throne for the Sinhalese. He ruled from Anuradhapura for ten years. However, his reign was also brought to an end by another invasion from South India, led by a Chola prince named Elara, who defeated and killed Asela to become the next ruler.
